title: Schemes of splittings of vector-bundle extensions preserve ordinary etale cohomology
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, let $\ell$ be a prime invertible on $X$, $n\geq1$, and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. Let $0\to E'\xrightarrow{j}E\xrightarrow{q}E''\to0$ be a short exact sequence of finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. Pullback is [def-pc-module-pullback]. The functor assigning to an $X$-scheme $f:Y\to X$ the set of $\mathcal O_Y$-linear maps $s:f^*E''\to f^*E$ with $(f^*q)s=1$ is represented by an $X$-scheme $\rho:S\to X$. It carries the universal such map, so the pulled-back sequence is split. It is Zariski locally isomorphic over $X$ to $\mathbf A_X^{ab}$, where $a=\operatorname{rank}E'$ and $b=\operatorname{rank}E''$ on that open [def-sbc-affine-space]; the translation between two sections is a unique map $f^*E''\to f^*E'$ via $f^*j$. In particular $S$ is Noetherian. In the ordinary small-etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], the adjunction unit $\Lambda_X\to R\rho_*\Lambda_S$ is an isomorphism. Consequently for every integer $t$ and every $q\geq0$ the canonical pullback $H^q(X,\Lambda(t))\to H^q(S,\Lambda(t))$ is an isomorphism, with the roots-of-unity twist identifications of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. No regularity or field-of-definition condition is imposed on $X$.

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 1.5 (Principe de scindage II), including its representing scheme and constant-coefficient derived unit; the twisted consequence uses the locally free Tate lines.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-local-splitting-finite-free] on the open rank strata, and refine its cover by affine opens trivializing $E\prime$ and $E\prime\prime$ as in [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. Thus on each chosen $U_i$ we have a section $s_i$ of $q$ and coordinates $E|_{U_i}\cong\mathcal O_{U_i}^{a_i}\oplus\mathcal O_{U_i}^{b_i}$ in which $j(v)=(v,0)$ and $q(v,w)=w$. Take a finite subcover, using quasi-compactness of $X$. Pullback in [def-pc-module-pullback] preserves these split identities: it sends $q s_i=1$, $j r_i+s_i q=1$ and $r_i j=1$ to the same identities. Hence the pulled-back sequence is exact and split on the inverse image of every $U_i$, for every test scheme; no flatness of the test morphism is required.

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 1.5, proof, printed page 227

proof.text: On $U_i$ form $S_i=\mathbf A^{a_i b_i}_{U_i}$. Let $T_i$ be its $a_i$ by $b_i$ matrix of coordinate functions. A test map $f:Y\to U_i$ and a section of $f^*q$ determine a matrix $(T,1)$ in the coordinates of step 1; conversely every such matrix is a section. By [lem-per-affine-space-global-functions] the matrix $T$ is precisely a unique $U_i$-morphism $Y\to S_i$. This proves representability on $U_i$, naturally for arbitrary test schemes, not only affine ones. The universal section is the column map $(T_i,1)$.

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 1.5, proof, printed page 227

proof.text: On $U_i\cap U_j$, change the two splittings and frames in step 1. In coordinates the matrix parameter changes by $T_j=A_{ij}T_iB_{ij}+C_{ij}$, with invertible frame matrices $A_{ij},B_{ij}$ and a translation matrix $C_{ij}$. Its entries are regular functions on the overlap, so [lem-per-affine-space-global-functions] makes it a morphism between the restrictions of $S_i,S_j$. Reversing the frame change is an inverse. On triple overlaps both composite changes send a section to its coordinates in the third frame, so uniqueness in that same bijection gives the cocycle identity. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-glue-schemes] to the open pieces lying over $U_i\cap U_j$. The projections agree on overlaps and glue by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] to $\rho:S\to X$. No affineness of $U_i\cap U_j$ is assumed.

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 1.5, proof, printed page 227

proof.text: For an arbitrary $f:Y\to X$, restrict to $f^{-1}U_i$. A section of $f^*q$ gives the local maps to $S_i$ in step 2; their changes are exactly those of step 3, so they glue uniquely to $Y\to S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. Conversely the local universal maps glue to a sheaf-module map: define its value on a local section by the maps on these opens, whose values agree on overlaps, and use the sheaf axiom. The two constructions are inverse since this is true on each $f^{-1}U_i$. Taking $Y=S$ gives the universal splitting. If $s,s\prime$ are two sections, then $q(s-s\prime)=0$. In the split coordinates of step 1 their difference is uniquely $(u,0)=j u$; these $u$ agree on overlaps by injectivity of $j$, and glue as sheaf maps. Thus translation is by a unique map $f^*E\prime\prime\to f^*E\prime$.

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 1.5, proof, printed page 227

proof.text: Every $U_i$ is Noetherian: it is affine, hence quasi-compact, and as an open subscheme of the locally Noetherian scheme $X$ it is locally Noetherian by the remark in [pqf-def-locnoeth]. By [def-amb-affine-trace-tower], its affine space $S_i$ is Noetherian, and the $d$-dimensional affine space is the tower of $d$ line projections with all intermediate stages Noetherian. The finitely many $S_i$ form an open cover of $S$. Their finite affine Noetherian covers together give a finite affine Noetherian cover of $S$, so $S$ is Noetherian by the definition in [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compactness of a finite union of quasi-compact subspaces. This includes $a_i b_i=0$ and the empty scheme.

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 1.5, proof, printed page 227

proof.text: We record explicitly the locality calculation used below. Choose a bounded-below injective resolution $F\to I$ of a constant-ring module sheaf on $S$, available by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. For an etale $v:V\to X$, identify the slice sites with the small etale sites by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open]; this identification also transports module actions. By [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], restriction is exact and right adjoint to exact extension by zero. It preserves injectives: a lifting problem into a restricted injective transposes to one into the injective along an extension-by-zero monomorphism. Thus $I|_{S_V}$ resolves $F|_{S_V}$. On an etale test object $W\to V$, the formulas of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] give the identical complexes $I(W\times_XS)$ for $(\rho_*I)|_V$ and $(\rho_V)_*(I|_{S_V})$. They therefore identify $(R\rho_*F)|_V$ with $R(\rho_V)_*(F|_{S_V})$. Under this comparison the restricted adjunction unit is the unit for $\rho_V$: both maps send a local coefficient section to its pullback on $W\times_XS$ and then to the resolution.

source.place: Locality needed in Proposition 1.5; module resolution argument using Stacks Tags 03DJ and 03F3

proof.text: For each Noetherian $U_i$, apply [lem-per-noetherian-affine-line-unit] at every stage of the $d=a_i b_i$ coordinate tower of [def-amb-affine-trace-tower]. Induct on $d$: $d=0$ is the identity. For $p_d:X_d\to U_i$ and $u_d:X_{d+1}\to X_d$, the unit for their composite is the unit for $p_d$ followed by $Rp_{d*}$ of the unit for $u_d$, under the canonical composition comparison of [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition](5). To check the actual map, transpose this composite under $u_d^{-1}p_d^{-1}\dashv Rp_{d*}Ru_{d*}$; the two triangle identities reduce its transpose to the identity of the pulled-back constant sheaf. By uniqueness of transposes it is the composite adjunction unit. Both factors are isomorphisms by induction and the affine-line input. Thus $\Lambda_{U_i}\to R(\rho|_{U_i})_*\Lambda_{S_i}$ is invertible for every $i$.

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 1.5, proof, printed page 227

proof.text: By step 6 the global constant-coefficient unit restricts to those of step 7. Every geometric point of $X$ lies in a $U_i$, so [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], applied to its cohomology-sheaf maps after forgetting module actions, makes these maps isomorphisms globally. A bijective module map has a module-linear inverse; hence [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] proves the desired module derived unit invertible. For a signed twist $L=\Lambda(t)$, [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] supplies an etale covering on which $L$ is free of rank one, and identifies $\rho^{-1}L$ with $\Lambda_S(t)$. Restrict simultaneously to this covering and the $U_i$. On a trivializing object the twisted unit is the constant unit by naturality. The constant unit there is already invertible: step 6 identifies it with restriction of the global constant unit just proved. The same stalk and cohomology criterion now proves $L\to R\rho_*\rho^{-1}L$ invertible. This requires no global root of unity on $X$ and no assumption that an etale trivializing object is Noetherian.

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 1.5, proof, printed page 227

proof.text: Apply derived global sections to the unit for $L=\Lambda(t)$ of step 8. Take a resolution $\rho^{-1}L\to J$ by injective objects $J^m$ ($m\geq0$) of $\operatorname{Mod}(S_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], $\rho^{-1}$ is exact and left adjoint to $\rho_*$ on module sheaves, with the unit of abelian sheaves; transposing monomorphism-lifting problems shows that $\rho_*$ preserves injective module sheaves. Thus $\rho_*J$ computes $R\rho_*\rho^{-1}L$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and by step 8 the composite $L\to\rho_*\rho^{-1}L\to\rho_*J$ is a quasi-isomorphism, i.e. a resolution of $L$. Cohomology in [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] is that of the underlying abelian sheaves. By clause (1) of [det-pbc-conventions-module-cohomology], the underlying abelian sheaves of the injective module sheaves $J^m$ on $S$ and $\rho_*J^m$ on $X$ have no higher cohomology. The acyclicity criterion (2) of [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity], for $\Gamma(X,-)$ and $\Gamma(S,-)$ on abelian sheaves, therefore gives natural isomorphisms $\mathcal H^q\Gamma(X,\rho_*J)\cong H^q(X,L)$ and $\mathcal H^q\Gamma(S,J)\cong H^q(S,\rho^{-1}L)$, induced by maps of resolutions $\varphi:\rho_*J\to I$ and $\psi:J\to J'$ over the identities into injective abelian resolutions. The equality $\Gamma(X,\rho_*J)=\Gamma(S,J)$ holds term by term by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. This gives $H^q(X,L)\cong H^q(S,\rho^{-1}L)$ for every $q\geq0$; with [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] its target is $H^q(S,\Lambda(t))$.

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 1.5, proof, printed page 227

proof.text: The isomorphism of step 9 is the pullback $\rho^*$ of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. There choose the injective abelian resolution $L\to I$ of step 9 and an injective abelian resolution $\rho^{-1}I\to J'$; this $J'$ resolves $\rho^{-1}L$ by exactness of $\rho^{-1}$, so take $\psi:J\to J'$ in step 9. Since $\rho^{-1}$ is exact, $\rho^{-1}\rho_*J$ resolves $\rho^{-1}L$. Two maps $\rho^{-1}\rho_*J\to J'$ over the identity of $\rho^{-1}L$ are compared: $\psi$ after the counit $\rho^{-1}\rho_*J\to J$, and $\rho^{-1}\varphi$ followed by $\rho^{-1}I\to J'$. Both become the same map in the derived category, since they agree after the quasi-isomorphism from $\rho^{-1}L$; as $J'$ is a bounded-below complex of injectives, hence K-injective, they are homotopic [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Precompose with the unit and take $\Gamma(X,-)$ of the adjoint maps. By the triangle identity the first gives $\Gamma(S,\psi)$ on $\Gamma(X,\rho_*J)=\Gamma(S,J)$. By naturality of the unit the second gives the pullback recipe of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] after $\Gamma(X,\varphi)$. Hence on cohomology the isomorphism of step 9 is $\rho^*$ under the identifications of step 9, for every $q\geq0$ and every integer $t$.
